chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you enter the mosque and the Imam is bowing (ruku'), and you think that if you walk to him he will raise his head before you catch up with him, then say Takbir and bow (ruku'), and when he raises his head, prostrate (sajdah) in your place. So if he stands, join the row, and if he sits, sit in your place. So when he stands, then join the row.

key_terms.رَاكِعٌ: bowing (state of the Imam in prayer)

ai.seo_question: What should a worshipper do if they enter the mosque while the Imam is bowing and they will not catch the bowing?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi addresses the specific scenario of 'fardah' (individual prayer) when entering late, prioritizing the preservation of the ruku' over strict row alignment. Shia jurists utilize this to distinguish between catching the Imam's ruku' as a pillar of prayer versus merely joining the congregation, emphasizing that the individual's prayer remains valid even if performed separately behind the row. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the integrity of individual ritual actions while maintaining communal order.
